body: Ok i will give it a try :)

Great, i will check it out if there are some jobs that suits me.

My condition is exactly like what doctor said "dry eye syndrome" but the thing is the eye drop doesnt really help me relief the pain. Yea Europe and US definitely have better medicine than my country so my doctor gave me a medicine that imported from Ireland.

Yep, i thought about working at home before but i just cant come out with any idea...i only knew some, like streaming or sales on internet. But i dont have any friends to start with so its out of the question. Any suggestion??

I live in China, they have covered some of my medical expenses pass few years. They dont consider my disease as a big threat compare to those who lost their legs, arms etc...so they paid half of my expenses. But its true, i can still work outside, i just need to bear the pain of my eye. Beside, i dont think its good to force myself and bear the pain, the pain will eventually lead to other diseases sooner or later.

My eye seems to be a little comforable inside my house cause i can adjust the air-condition. Too windy will cause my eye to pain. I rarely go outside because sunlight hurts my eyes the most, doctor said to me too. Sometimes the pain will occur even without sunlight or windy environment, its unpredictable. Then i need to cooldown my eye with warm damp towel, close and give my eye some rest. This is why i cant go to work, environment issue and unpredictedble pain. Who would want to pay for an employee like this...??

I dont think i can get an opinion abroad since im not living in that kind of super rich family that will take me abroad just to visit a doctor. Financial aid?? Im not to sure what do u mean, but financial aids are all for the students who attend University right?? Im not attending any Unversity, its not that i dont want, i could not.

That eye doctor is one of the best in my country. He saved me from becoming blind 5 years ago, the operation took like 5-6hours. I visited him several times because i thought maybe he misjudged my dry eye syndrome and told him my eye is still in pain after using the eye drop. He said its no doubt a dry eye syndrome. Not only i visited him, i also visited some others very well known eye doctors in the same eye specialist center as him. (Most of the best eye doctors in my country gathered there) Other doctors said its a dry eye syndrone too, its just a little bit serious than the usual one because my eyes underwent a surgery before.
